newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand policeman admits faking assault.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand policeman admits faking assault.

text.p: A detective with New Zealand's police fraud squad on Wednesday admitted faking an attempt on his life and burning down his own home to make a false insurance claim.

Brent Garner, a detective in the North Island town of Palmerston North, was remanded in custody for sentencing on December 13 after pleading guilty to eight charges relating to the October 18 incident.
The case was originally reported as a horrendous assault on Garner and a miraculous escape.
Prosecutor Ben Vanderkolk told the court that some time this year, Garner decided to liquidate his assets, separate from his wife and change his life.

Early one October morning, he spread petrol throughout his home and cut his own back with a scalpel. He then set a timing device, threw petrol over himself, tied a gag over his mouth and tied himself up.
After the home was engulfed in fire, Garner was found near the house, still bound and gagged, with multiple injuries and claiming to have escaped his attackers.
After 37 days of police investigation, Garner admitted he had staged the whole affair.
He said he did it to give his wife a good financial start and ensure his family would be taken care of.
But Garner's wife Sandra later said in a radio interview that all her husband wanted was to end their marriage.
"But he didn't have the guts or the balls to tell me directly," she said. Instead, he did "this devious and evil thing" and hurt a great many people, she said.
